correctness.rationale: For 0≤t<N=p^a, the digits of N−1−t are the complements of the a digits of t. The two multiples (q−1)(N−1) and q(N−1) split into complementary length-a blocks (q−2,N−q+1) and (q−1,N−q), respectively. Both therefore have digit sum a(p−1) for the full range 2≤q≤N, including q=N. Legendre’s formula gives exact valuation a. Newton interpolation of F(X)=binom(kX,k) at 1 through k+1 gives F(0)≡k+1 modulo a common prime divisor of F(2),…,F(k+1), so p is the only possible prime in the gcd and the gcd is N. Independent exact binomial and factorial-valuation checks agreed across 11 prime powers through N=32, 136 individual terms, and all 11 gcds; replay: branches/4cc28ef1-1243-41ac-b84c-830949427918/bounded-repro.py. The finite replay is not the proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For every higher level j=a+h (h≥1), the displayed X gives [X]_{p^{a+h}}=N[q−1]_{p^h}+N−q, since 0≤N−q<N. As [k]_{p^{a+h}}=N−1, the prior residue test is true exactly when [q−1]_{p^h}=0: if nonzero the residue is at least N, and if zero it equals N−q<N−1. There are therefore exactly t high levels and a−t low ones. This is direct substitution in the earlier proof’s formulas, with no further estimate or structural lemma.
